title: Q3 Mobile App Product Review
segments: Welcome everyone. This is our Q3 review for the mobile app. I'll start with the numbers, then Priya will share what customers are telling us, and we'll finish with Q4 priorities.
Weekly active users are up twenty-two percent quarter over quarter, to about eleven thousand. Push notification opt-in is at sixty-one percent, which is above our target of fifty-five.
What's driving the growth? Is it new customers or existing ones adopting the app?
Mostly existing. About seventy percent of the new actives are drivers and dispatchers at customers who already had accounts. The share of new accounts is small.
The less good news is retention. Thirty-day retention for new users is only forty-one percent, and we're aiming for fifty-five.
Do we know where people drop off? I'd guess onboarding.
Yes. Our funnel shows thirty-four percent of new users abandon during the carrier connection step. It asks for a lot of information up front.
That matches what I saw in the usability sessions in August. People didn't understand why we needed their carrier credentials before showing them any value.
We could let people explore with demo data first and then ask for credentials when they want to see their own shipments. That's maybe a week of work on my side.
I like that. I'd also shorten the form. We ask for seven fields and I think we only need three to get started.
Let's make that a candidate for Q4. Priya, what are you hearing from customers?
The top request by far is offline support. Drivers lose signal in rural areas and the app just spins. We had nineteen tickets about it last quarter.
Second is notification control. Dispatchers get alerts for every shipment, and they want to mute everything except exceptions.
And third, which surprised me, is the map. People love it but say it's slow on older Android phones.
The map slowness is real. We render every marker even when they're off screen. Clustering and a viewport query would fix most of it.
Probably two weeks including testing on low end devices. The offline support is much bigger, more like six to eight weeks, because we have to design the sync model.
Then I'd put the map performance and onboarding changes first, and treat offline as the big bet for the second half of the quarter.
Priya, would customers accept that ordering? Offline is the loudest request.
I think so if we're upfront. I'd suggest a short note to the nineteen customers who filed tickets saying it's planned and giving a rough date.
Agreed. I'll draft something and run it past you before it goes out.
Let me show the new design for notification settings. I mocked up a simple three-level control: everything, exceptions only, and nothing.
Under that there's an advanced section for per-customer rules. I kept it collapsed by default so most people never see it.
That looks clean. Does it need backend changes?
A little. We need to store the preference per user and have the notification service respect it. Marcus estimated three days on the backend.
Good, so that's a small win we can ship early in the quarter. What about the dark mode request?
It's mostly done on the design side. The tokens are defined, and Sofia has started wiring them up for the web app, so mobile can reuse the same set.
Right, but I wouldn't promise it for mobile this quarter. It depends on whether the navigation rewrite happens.
Where are we on the navigation rewrite? I remember we deferred it in Q2.
It's still deferred. The current structure makes deep links hard, which is why our notification taps sometimes land on the wrong screen.
That's actually something customers notice. We've had a handful of complaints about tapping an alert and ending up on the home screen.
Then it's not just internal cleanup. Aisha, can you size it as a customer facing fix and not a refactor?
Yes, I'll reframe it around deep link reliability and bring a proposal to planning next week.
Let me pull together the Q4 priorities so we're clear. One, onboarding simplification. Two, map performance. Three, notification controls.
Four, navigation rewrite for deep links, if the proposal holds up. And five, offline support as the large bet, with design starting in week four.
What are the success metrics? I'd like to commit to something specific.

Thirty-day retention at fifty percent by end of quarter, down from forty-one. Carrier connection abandonment under twenty percent, and map load time under two seconds on a three-year-old Android phone.
Can we also track something qualitative? I'd like a monthly check in with five or six drivers to see how the app actually feels in their day.
I can recruit those. A few of our customers have already offered.
Good. Any risks I should know about?
Capacity. If offline starts in week four and navigation lands at the same time, I'm the bottleneck on both. We might need to borrow someone from the web side.
Noted. I'll talk to the leads about that, but let's not assume it. Can we sequence navigation before offline instead?
That makes sense, since offline sync benefits from a cleaner navigation structure anyway.
I'll update the plan. So navigation lands in weeks three to six, and offline design runs in parallel, with build starting after.
Works for me. Anything else before we wrap?
One request. Can we add a status page link inside the app? When carrier connectors are down, customers file support tickets because they think the app is broken.
Easy to add. I'll sketch a small banner that appears when a connector is degraded.
Great, I'll add that to the Q4 list as a small item. Thanks everyone, I'll send out the notes and the plan by tomorrow.
Thanks all. This was a productive one.
overview: Quarterly review of the mobile app. Weekly active users grew 22% to about 11,000, but 30-day retention for new users is 41% against a 55% goal, largely because 34% abandon at the carrier connection step. Customer feedback centres on offline support, notification control, and slow maps on older Android phones. The team agreed Q4 priorities: simplify onboarding, speed up the map with clustering, ship a three-level notification control, rewrite navigation to fix unreliable deep links, and start offline support as the large bet. Success metrics were set at 50% retention, under 20% connection abandonment, and map load under two seconds. Navigation was sequenced ahead of offline to avoid overloading Sofia.
